requirements.quote:
The format of these files is a sequence of entries.  Entries are
predominantly line-oriented, though parentheses can be used to continue
a list of items across a line boundary, and text literals can contain
CRLF within the text.  Any combination of tabs and spaces act as a
delimiter between the separate items that make up an entry.  The end of
any line in the master file can end with a comment.  The comment starts
with a ";" (semicolon).
requirements.condition: When reading a master file.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the file as a sequence of entries.
requirements.why_checkable: The loader can be checked for sequential entry parsing.

requirements.quote:
Two control entries are defined: $ORIGIN and $INCLUDE.  $ORIGIN is
followed by a domain name, and resets the current origin for relative
domain names to the stated name.  $INCLUDE inserts the named file into
the current file, and may optionally specify a domain name that sets the
relative domain name origin for the included file.  $INCLUDE may also
have a comment.  Note that a $INCLUDE entry never changes the relative
origin of the parent file, regardless of changes to the relative origin
made within the included file.
requirements.condition: When processing a $INCLUDE entry naming a file.
requirements.required_behavior: Insert the named file into the current file.
requirements.why_checkable: Records from the named file can be checked at the include position.

requirements.quote: $INCLUDE <file-name> [<domain-name>] [<comment>]
requirements.condition: When parsing a $INCLUDE entry.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit omission of the domain-name argument.
requirements.why_checkable: An include entry containing only the filename is an explicitly allowed form.

requirements.quote:
<character-string> is expressed in one or two ways: as a contiguous set
of characters without interior spaces, or as a string beginning with a "
and ending with a ".  Inside a " delimited string any character can
occur, except for a " itself, which must be quoted using \ (back slash).
requirements.condition: When reading an unquoted master-file character-string.
requirements.required_behavior: Accept a contiguous set of characters without interior spaces as a character-string.
requirements.why_checkable: A contiguous unquoted token can be checked as a character-string value.

requirements.required_behavior: Recognize a string beginning and ending with double-quote delimiters.
requirements.why_checkable: Paired double quotes delimit a concrete alternative character-string syntax.

requirements.condition: When a free-standing @ occurs in a master file.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret @ as the current origin.
requirements.why_checkable: The resulting name can be compared with the current origin.

requirements.quote:
\X              where X is any character other than a digit (0-9), is

requirements.condition: When a backslash is followed by a character X other than a digit from 0 through 9.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret X as a quoted literal character whose special meaning does not apply.
requirements.why_checkable: Escaped punctuation can be decoded and checked to remain label or text content instead of syntax.

requirements.quote:
\DDD            where each D is a digit is the octet corresponding to
                the decimal number described by DDD.  The resulting
                octet is assumed to be text and is not checked for
                special meaning.
requirements.condition: When a master-file escape has the form backslash followed by three decimal digits DDD.
requirements.required_behavior: Decode the escape as the octet corresponding to the decimal number DDD.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded byte can be compared with the decimal value of the three digits.

requirements.quote:
\DDD            where each D is a digit is the octet corresponding to

                octet is assumed to be text and is not checked for

requirements.condition: When an octet results from a backslash-DDD escape.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the resulting octet as text.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Check the resulting octet for special meaning.
requirements.why_checkable: Numeric escapes of syntax characters can be checked to remain literal text.

requirements.quote:
( )             Parentheses are used to group data that crosses a line
                boundary.  In effect, line terminations are not
                recognized within parentheses.
requirements.condition: When master-file data is grouped within parentheses across a line boundary.
requirements.required_behavior: Continue the grouped data across line boundaries.
requirements.why_checkable: A parenthesized entry spanning multiple lines can be checked as one continued data group.

requirements.quote:
;               Semicolon is used to start a comment; the remainder of
                the line is ignored.
requirements.condition: When a semicolon starts a master-file comment.
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the remainder of the line.
requirements.why_checkable: Content after the comment delimiter can be checked to have no effect on parsed data.
